name: Herod
description: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament

points: Herod hears of him and says it is John, whom he beheaded, risen from the dead.

note.label: Mark 6: A Prophet Without Honour, the Death of John, and the Five Thousand

points: John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

note.label: Mark 6: A Prophet Without Honour, the Death of John, and the Five Thousand

points: Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod. They reason among themselves that it is because they have no bread.

note.label: Mark 8: The Four Thousand, the Confession of Peter, and the Cross

points: The fourth feather: Caligula, born AD 12, died AD 41, reign AD 37 to 41, the first Roman emperor to be assassinated; initiated construction of Roman aqueducts. Within the book of Acts his reign roughly corresponds to Acts 7 (the death of Stephen) through early Acts 12: the persecution following Stephen's death and Saul's conversion (circa AD 35 to 36), Peter's vision and ministry in Acts 10 and 11 around the time Caligula's persecution of Jews in Alexandria prompted a crisis, and Acts 12 (the death of James and the imprisonment of Peter under Herod Agrippa I) just after Caligula's assassination.
Herod, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evils which he had done, added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.

note.label: Luke 3: The Preaching of John and the Generations Back to Adam

points: Herod is perplexed, hearing that John was risen from the dead, or that Elias had appeared, and says, John have I beheaded: but who is this?

note.label: Luke 9: The Twelve Sent, the Confession, and the Cost of Following

points: Herod was exceeding glad, hoping to have seen some miracle done by him, and questioned him in many words, but he answered him nothing.

note.label: Luke 23: The Trial, the Crucifixion, and the Burial

points: For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together. So Herod, an Edomite, a white man that was set up by Rome to rule Jerusalem. And Pontius Pilate, another leader set up by Rome. With the Gentiles. And the people of Israel, the religious leaders. They were gathered together against Christ. Antichrist. Why? Because Herod understood, he killed thousands of black babies to prevent Christ from being born. That is antichrist. Because he knew that Christ was supposed to come, and Christ is the king, and he would not be ruling any more. The white man would not be ruling any more. So ever since Christ was born, the antichrist system was set up.

Being let go, they went to their own company and reported all, and they lifted up their voice to God with one accord: Lord, thou art God who made heaven and earth; why did the heathen rage and the people imagine vain things; the kings of the earth stood up and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. Against the holy child Jesus, Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel were gathered together, and this same thing is going to happen all over again.

cases.name: Herod Antipas and Herodias
cases.charge: Taking his brother’s wife; beheading John for saying so
cases.preview: Herod the tetrarch had married Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, and John told him plainly that it was not lawful for him to have his brother’s wife (Mark 6:17-18).
